new.s: Elections to panchayats and municipalities in India are conducted by which body?
o: The Election Commission of India under Article 324
State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA
The Chief Electoral Officer of the State under Article 325
new.x: Panchayat and municipal polls are run by the State Election Commissions under Articles 243K (panchayats) and 243ZA (municipalities), not by the ECI. Article 324 vests control of Parliament, State legislature, President and VP elections in the ECI; Article 325 provides one general electoral roll; Article 329 bars courts in electoral matters. The CEO and Delimitation Commission do not conduct local polls.
new.tq: Local bodies = SEC: 243K (panchayat), 243ZA (municipality).

new.s: The voting age in India was lowered from 21 to 18 years by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
new.x: The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 amended Article 326 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18 (in force 1989). The 42nd Amendment (1976) froze seat allocation on the 1971 Census, the 52nd (1985) added the anti-defection Tenth Schedule, and the 73rd (1992) dealt with panchayats.
new.tq: 61st = 18 to vote (1988).

new.s: The freeze on the inter-State allocation of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 1971 Census was first imposed by which Amendment, and until when?
new.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) froze inter-State seat allocation on the 1971 Census till 2000 to encourage population control. The 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze till the first census after 2026, and the 87th (2003) switched boundary redrawing to the 2001 Census. The 44th Amendment did not deal with the freeze.
new.tq: 42nd froze (1971 Census, till 2000); 84th extended (till 2026); 87th = 2001 Census boundaries.

Article 334 originally set 10 years (till 1960). The 95th Amendment gave the previous extension; the 106th introduced one-third women's reservation (Art 334A); the 84th dealt with the delimitation freeze.
new.tq: 104th: SC/ST seats to 2030 + Anglo-Indian nomination ended.

new.s:
Consider the following conditions for recognition as a National Party:
1. Recognised as a State party in four or more States
2. 6% of valid votes in four States plus four Lok Sabha seats
3. 2% of Lok Sabha seats from at least three States
Which of the above is/are valid conditions (any one sufficing)?
new.x: All three are alternative criteria under the Election Symbols Order, 1968: State-party recognition in 4+ States; 6% votes in 4 States plus 4 Lok Sabha seats; or 2% of Lok Sabha seats from at least 3 States. The APPSC-G2 2025 question on these conditions keyed 'None of the above' as the invalid one. Options A, B and C each leave out a valid criterion.
new.tq: National party: 4 States recognised OR 6%x4 States + 4 LS seats OR 2% LS seats from 3 States.

new.x: The Lok Satta Party was founded by Jayaprakash Narayan in 2006, not Pawan Kalyan, so D is wrongly matched. The YSRCP was founded by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy in March 2011 after a split from Congress, Jana Sena by Pawan Kalyan in 2014, and the TRS (now BRS) by K. Chandrashekar Rao in 2001.
new.tq: YSRCP 2011 Jagan; JSP 2014 Pawan; TRS 2001 KCR; Lok Satta 2006 JP.
